content.v: 在育碧任职五年的Raashi Sikka宣布，她将出任公司首席AI赋能官。她此前负责多元、包容、无障碍及社会影响事务。此次职务调整正值育碧推进生成式AI项目Motherbrain。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791578454_271854_jpg_r.jpg
Sikka表示AI将改变技术、文化、社会及工作方式。她希望帮助公司和团队做好准备，更有信心地应对变化，同时关注这些变化对人的影响。
育碧近期在内部宣布，Motherbrain将作为覆盖全公司的全球性实体运作。10月7日育碧向员工介绍了该项目的新定位：一个致力于将生成式AI转化为实际游戏体验的专门团队。
对于生成式AI在开发中的角色，育碧管理层将其定位为创作工具，而非编剧、设计师或演员的替代品。Motherbrain总经理Xavier Manzanares举例说，这项技术在部分游戏中可能用于可交谈的角色、能适应玩家计划的队友或自主运转的世界。在另一些游戏中，则可能用于改进角色行为、引导新玩家或无障碍体验。公司内部预期，各团队今后都会探索Motherbrain及生成式AI。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

news.title: 前PS高管更偏好20至25小时游戏 认为百小时流程并非全程精彩
news.summary: 前索尼互动娱乐全球工作室首席执行官Shawn Layden在Expansion Pass播客中表示，他更希望看到游玩时长为20至25小时、节奏紧凑且能持续吸引玩家的游戏。在他看来，长达80、90乃至100小时的作品，并非

content.v: 前索尼互动娱乐全球工作室首席执行官Shawn Layden在Expansion Pass播客中表示，他更希望看到游玩时长为20至25小时、节奏紧凑且能持续吸引玩家的游戏。在他看来，长达80、90乃至100小时的作品，并非每一段流程都有同等质量。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791577511_577475_jpg_r.jpg
Layden说自己玩过这些长篇作品，并举出为了取得一件道具而长距离往返的例子，说明游戏流程可能怎样被拉长。他主张重新关注范围更清晰的项目，而不是单纯追求更长的游玩时间。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791577512_660253_jpg_r.jpg
谈到开发成本时，Layden认为，如果团队以较小规模的作品为目标，成本即使不能下降，至少也可能停止继续上涨。这是他对开发方向的判断，并非已经得到验证的成本变化。
Layden还将部分延长游戏流程的做法与20世纪90年代的游戏租赁文化联系起来。他说，当时开发者会设法让玩家无法在一个周末的租期内通关。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

news.summary: 近日法国游戏博主J0nathan的油管频道遭到平台永久封禁，导火索是恐怖游戏《猛鬼追魂：复苏》游戏实机视频。即便他已用黑块遮挡了视频内裸露画面，账号依旧被封。 《猛鬼追魂：复苏》开场包含尺度较大的亲密、BDSM相关镜头，

content.v: 近日法国游戏博主J0nathan的油管频道遭到平台永久封禁，导火索是恐怖游戏《猛鬼追魂：复苏》游戏实机视频。即便他已用黑块遮挡了视频内裸露画面，账号依旧被封。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791577357_266581_jpg_r.jpg
《猛鬼追魂：复苏》开场包含尺度较大的亲密、BDSM相关镜头，该段情节是推动整个故事的关键剧情铺垫。博主给视频打上“不适合儿童”标签，但没有开启平台的年龄门槛限制，他原本以为对裸露画面打码就可以规避平台规则处罚。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791578426_141478.jpg
封禁发生前，该频道拥有19万订阅，积攒了十年内容、超过3000条视频，也是博主主要收入来源。博主表示在此之前账号从未收到过任何警告或者违规处罚，直接永久封禁的处理方式让他难以接受。
J0nathan提交申诉但油管很快驳回，平台给出官方理由：平台禁止以获得性满足为目的的露骨内容。博主质疑审核偏向AI自动处理，缺少人工复核，同样这段未打码的游戏片段，却依旧可以在其他部分油管账号正常播放。这件事也引发创作者社区讨论：成熟向游戏片段该如何界定审核标准、申诉机制是否存在缺陷。博主表示自己正在考虑依据欧盟《数字服务法案》采取进一步法律行动。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 欧洲消费者保护机构已针对10家游戏公司采取协调执法行动，重点审视游戏内消费是否透明、公平。行动由意大利竞争管理机构牵头，在欧盟委员会协调下推进；有关机构尤其关注未成年人及可能受到游戏成瘾影响的消费者能否看清实际支出。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791577073_280922_jpg_r.jpg
此次行动关注固定面额的虚拟货币礼包与商品价格不匹配的问题。玩家购买一件商品时，可能必须先买入超过所需数量的游戏币。可能诱导消费的界面设计、家长控制机制不足及客户支持问题，也在关注范围内。
行动涉及动视暴雪、Crytek、InnoGames、King、Mojang、Plarium、Riot Games、Supercell和育碧等公司。其中，动视暴雪是主要关注对象，《暗黑破坏神：不朽》等作品被特别提及，相关关注延续了此前的调查。
《堡垒之夜》将从10月14日起允许玩家按需购买游戏货币。类似调整也将扩展至另外两款游戏及多个平台，但目前不包括PlayStation。此次执法行动最终会带来哪些规则变化，仍取决于后续进展。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 近日R星叙事高级副总裁鲁珀特·汉弗莱斯谈到《《GTA6》主角杰森·杜瓦尔的犯罪动机时表示，杰森抢劫银行等行为与他的物质处境有关。环境造成了多大影响、其中又有多少出于个人选择，玩家可以自行判断。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260924/1790196228_477186_jpg_r.jpg
杰森在犯罪者身边长大，曾为了摆脱问题重重的少年时期而入伍。后来他回到罪恶 都市 外的Leonida Keys，为当地毒贩工作。这些经历为理解他的现状提供了线索，但汉弗莱斯在采访中没有说明杰森本人如何看待过去。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791576647_105107_jpg_r.jpg
汉弗莱斯使用的“wired differently”一词也引出一些玩家对杰森特质或隐藏身份的猜测。采访并未证实这些解读，不能将其视为已公布的人物设定。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261010/1791576648_215223_jpg_r.jpg
杰森想过轻松的生活，另一位主角露西亚·卡米诺斯则被R星写成决心为自己争取更好未来的人。两人目标不同，采访未透露这会如何影响他们的合作关系。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

news.title: LucasFilm Games Producer Responds after Galactic Racer Character Biddy Blas Goes Viral
news.summary: If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making t

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/09/biddy-blas-scrib-doon-1791575939855.jpg

If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas.

It’s almost impossible to hate the guy, who tells you all about how awesome he is in a hilarious spiel that has somehow become everyone’s new vocal stim. In Huttese, Blas tells you: “Here’s a name for you, amateur! Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!”

However, it’s the fantastic voice acting behind this line that’s got players cracking up. “Biddy Blas! Scrib doon!” is an undeniable banger, and I personally cannot stop saying it in response to basically anything. (My poor friend group is already tired of it.)
This Star Wars: Galactic Racer voice acting though! 💀🤣 https://t.co/oYkTMT2nSf

Posts of Blas introducing himself have gone viral on social media, to the point where they caught the attention of LucasFilm Games Producer Craig Derrick, who responded to the overwhelming influx of love for Blas on Twitter/X.

“It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer!” he wrote. “Thank you for all the kind words! Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it.”

Biddy Blas is a Crocin who, as players have come to find out, will literally do whatever it takes to win… even if that means giving you a ‘gift’ that’s actually a bomb, which, if you accept it, will explode your ship and give your opponents a major head start.

It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer! Thank you for all the kind words! 🙏 Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it. 😂 https://t.co/SdXjIq9HkF
Hate him or love him, the guy’s the talk of the town right now, with some fans affectionately dubbing him the “glup shitto of the year.”
“I would like to say I'd die for Biddy Blas, but at the same time, I have also slammed him into a wall at like 500mph multiple times at this stage,” one fan joked .
“Biddy Blas is hilarious, I'm going to kill him,” another said after their speeder got blown up thanks to accepting Blas’s ‘gift.’

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been a major hit with Star Wars fans and critics alike, with IGN’s Luke Reilly scoring the game an eight out of ten. “Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that gets a little repetitive thanks to its heavy reliance on repeatedly revisiting the same slim selection of planets, but has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe,” he wrote in our review .

It’s a good time to be a pod racer, as developer Fuse Games recently announced that Galactic Racer’s multiplayer party limit will soon double in size in a post-launch patch coming in the next few weeks.

news.title: Don't worry, Valve: I've got your next Deadlock character concepts sorted
news.summary: The Cursed Apple is ready for Humpty Dumpty and the Loch Ness Monster's Precocious Preteen Child.

content.v: Deadlock is one of the most delightful things happening in videogame art direction. It's a festival of phenomenal vibes: a striking setting, an all-timer aesthetic that bleeds into every scrap of environmental art and UI element, and—crucially—a roster of instantly charming occult character designs.

That roster, however, is missing something—a few somethings, in fact. While Deadlock's heroes cover a broad spectrum of the spooky and supernatural, it's got some glaring gaps where foundational elements of cryptozoology and occult lore are sorely overlooked. But don't fret, Valve designers: I've done your next round of ideation for you. I've prepared some promising character concepts that, I think we'll all agree, will realize the Cursed Apple's untapped potential. Let's begin:
The Summer Mummy (from Heathcliff)
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/33SZW6AhUiX636MeDHFmm4-1920-80.jpg

Deadlock's already got draculas. It's got werewolves. It's got a Frankenstein. When you're already this deep in monster mash territory, a mummy's a layup. It's Spooky Stuff 101. The problem, however, is that it's not enough to be just a mummy in New York. New York is where they make cool people. If you're going to hang with the Cursed Apple's finest, you're going to need style.

Enter the Summer Mummy, a character first introduced in Heathcliff—the comic strip about the orange cat who isn't Garfield—on August 17, 2023 . The Summer Mummy is much like your typical bandaged revenant, except chill and fun. He wears floral boardshorts. He has sunglasses. He eats ice cream ( the Summer Mummy gets the sand flavor ). He's an instant crowd pleaser, and it's an incredible cross-promotional opportunity. Everyone's trying to tap the lucrative Heathcliff brand.
A minotaur who plays baseball professionally
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/LXo7fuxHE8avFatFJJ4mBf-1920-80.jpg

Just to be clear: No, I didn't come up with this one because "bullpen" is a baseball thing. I just thought a minotaur in an old-timey baseball uniform would look sick. I only realized the bullpen bit afterwards—but as far as I'm concerned, that was me getting a thumbs up from an angel for my very good work.

What was the labyrinth if not the most mythological bullpen of them all? The minotaur might've been warming up his pitching arm down there. Gotta pass the time somehow. Oh! He could throw a curveball that follows a nonsense, labyrinthine path through the air. Call it a Daedalian Knuckleball or something. Give him a bull rush ability called "charge the mound." Stuff writes itself. Put my check in the mail.
The Loch Ness Monster's precocious preteen child
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hN5dEvSdtULk3TT3JWePz8-1920-80.jpg

There's a lot to love about this one: First, Nessie is already confirmed Deadlock canon , having arrived on Earth through the Bermuda Triangle astral gate. Second, there's never a bad time for more Scottish accents. Third, they could be buddies with Rem, Deadlock's adorable sleepspace creature.

But what really makes Nessie Jr. (legally, that name might be taken ) a winner is the microtransaction potential: Give this kid a character lunchbox, and once Deadlock starts rolling out purchasable skins, people will pay whatever you ask just to see different fictional licensed properties slapped on there. It's infinite money.
Three gnomes in a trench coat
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/u7sqLkGHAVsDan2xjHDVhe-1920-80.jpg

I'll confess: I don't have a lot to flesh this entry out with. Mostly, I just think it would be neat for all of them to have little guns under there. Maybe they're in the mob? A gnome mafia. The Cosa Gnomestra. I don't know. Do your best.
A haunted suit of armor (who is a boxer)
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gGikJ74oYzrCEk3nVbEmpZ-1920-80.jpg

Everyone loves an animated suit of armor. Much like with the Summer Mummy, however, there's some aesthetic work that needs to be done to bring the image in line with Deadlock's aesthetic theme. And much like with the Summer Mummy, I've identified a shorts-centric solution—boxing shorts, in this case. And boxing gloves. A plate armor prize fighter who could play like the third-person MOBA-shooter equivalent of Little Mac.

Now, you might ask, does Deadlock need yet another prize fighter when it already has Lash and Bebop? And to that I'd say: Neither of them has cartoonishly big shorts, do they? It's like you're not even paying attention.
Big spider
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/E5xe3H8JoXxq3wMxgjAyJD-1920-80.jpg

There was, admittedly, already an unreleased spider-themed hero during Deadlock's Hero Labs days, but frankly, why half-ass it? Just go full spider. Let it walk on all the surfaces. Give it eight weapons for each of its eight limbs. Is it really a videogame if there isn't a large enemy spider in there somewhere?
Big spider (sexy)
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/iXGXixGMVnRNnzfXNoSk2P-1920-80.jpeg
I can't take credit for this one:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ffKTUYUJZvUDdCbNxmaz7J-1920-80.png
Humpty Dumpty
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pV3fEaM5EpYJbEqMGdTucm-1920-80.jpg

We all know the deal: on wall, great fall, horses and men prove inadequate at reconstructive surgery, etc. But I'm imagining this is the Humpty Dumpty that's had to go on living knowing the world failed him in his darkest moment—a sort of Punished "Venom" Dumpty situation. He's fighting in the Ritual not to restore his own broken form, but to create a world for other shattered eggs like himself. It's the kind of grim antihero that audiences crave.
And he could, like, roll around to attack sometimes, maybe. That's fun.
The rest of the monkey that the Monkey's Paw came off of
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/y8K84x9z9VbcShbyMtEvrS-1920-80.jpg

That thing had to come from somewhere, right? If the Paw can grant wishes, imagine what all the other parts of the enchanted monkey must be capable of. Surely, it must have been severed from the limb of a sort of simian arch-sorcerer, who possessed a command over magicks so profound as to reconfigure the flow of fate itself.
What I'm saying is he could shoot energy balls from his stump like it was a Mega Man arm cannon and it would rule. And maybe he does street magic in Times Square. For walking around money.
North Pole elf labor rights activist
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4d8wwx4dCxUHmsNFXMk3y7-1920-80.jpg

I think we've all known it for a long time: There's something untoward about the whole Santa Claus operation. We're meant to believe that an entire society is content with knowing no life beyond the ceaseless churn of toy production under the rule of a treat-crazed overlord? Really?

I don't buy it—and that's exactly why there's a hero who's ventured to New York to foster awareness and support for the plight of their fellows still trapped toiling at the Kringle company town up north. They could create a bunch of nutcracker soldiers as their ult, but they'd be nutcracker soldiers of the revolution.

One of the deer from Staten Island, but it was turned into a sapient anthropoid by some sort of cursed amulet and is struggling to adjust to city life on account of antlers making it hard to get into buildings
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vHUcgxZXX7HiZWn4gSosTK-1920-80.jpg
Label sorta says it all, really.
Bigfoot (he is running for mayor)

It just makes sense. He's a compelling figure. He's all-American. He's privacy conscious and likely has a sensible platform regarding municipal walkability. He's been around long enough that he probably knows a few spells, and he's big enough that he could handle a Lewis gun like an airsoft rifle.
He'd have my vote, is what I'm saying. And the best part is: You'd be able to listen to the other heroes grill Bigfoot about his political stances. That's videogames to me.

news.title: Skate Developer Promises More Creative Tools Are Coming After ReSkate Modding Platform Goes Viral
news.summary: Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launc

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/09/skate-developer-addresses-reskate-1791574192606.jpg
Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate.

ReSkate was officially released into the wild about a week ago. This platform allows fans to play the game offline, create private servers, make their own maps, and more. It’s already been downloaded over 350,000 times on GitHub, and its creators are well-aware that they might get hit with a cease-and-desist order.

However, that doesn’t seem to be a problem — at least, not yet, but the devs at Full Circle aren’t exactly toothless about the situation, either. Full Circle published a statement acknowledging fan mods on October 9, where they admitted to the importance of community mods while also standing firm against those that bypass paid cosmetics or make money off of new features.

“Skateboarding in general is built on community and creative expression, and we support that. We love seeing your passion for pushing the limits of San Vansterdam in different ways. That's why we built our new skateboarding sandbox in San Vansterdam to begin with, to give you, the players, the tools you need to have fun and create amazing content,” it wrote.

“To be completely clear, we are not against creativity from players or stopping that from happening. Where we have to draw the line is when mods or other tools bypass our systems to unlock paid cosmetics, release gated/unreleased content, or profit from these unauthorized assets. That rips off the artists, skate brands, and creators, as well as our own development team here at Full Circle, who work hard to bring skate culture into our game.

Full Circle went on to confirm that it is aware that players want “more freedom and custom features,” and revealed that it’s currently building “official, secure access tools that enable broader, deeper community creation.” More news on this will be shared at a later date.
A message from the team at Full Circle regarding mods and community content. https://t.co/sTiTUvkRWX

ReSkate’s popularity is undeniable; after its release, Skate’s playerbase saw a massive jump in active players, peaking at over 7,000 players on October 5 — the highest it’s been for months after the game's launch in September 2025.
Speaking with PC Gamer , the developers of ReSkate admitted that they “honestly didn't realize how big this was going to be," saying they were “just doing it for the love of the game."

They also told the outlet that they are prepared to take ReSkate down if EA’s lawyers come knocking, which many fans are already assuming will happen at some point down the line. For now, though, ReSkate remains alive and well, and it has seemingly spurred Full Circle into taking action to give the game more community-friendly features.

news.title: Call Of Duty: MW4 Early Access Also Includes DMZ, Here’s How To Get In
news.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's campaign is playable a week early for people who preorder, and now we know th

content.v: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's campaign is playable a week early for people who preorder, and now we know the DMZ mode will be as well.

Activision has announced that MW4's extraction-based DMZ mode will be playable starting Tuesday, October 20, which is three days before the game launches. Campaign early access, meanwhile, starts on October 16.
How to get in
To access DMZ mode before everyone else, you need to preorder any edition of MW4, including the standard or Vault versions. The perk applies to all platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC.
What is DMZ?

Described as the "definitive extraction shooter experience," DMZ in MW4 is an open-world game mode featuring other human players and AI combatants. Players will search the map for loot, craft gear, and complete objectives. Like in other extraction-based games, you need to reach the exfil point to make it out with all your rewards.

DMZ originally debuted with 2022's MW3 as a free-to-play beta inside Warzone, but this version left a lot to be desired. The new version of DMZ for MW4 seems like a big step up , and it includes a new social space this time as well.
For lots more, be sure to read up on GameSpot's previous coverage of the new version of DMZ .

news.title: Gears Of War: E-Day–How’s It Selling? Let’s Unpack Things
news.summary: Microsoft's latest console exclusive, Gears of War: E-Day , launched this week, and now we've gotten the first

content.v: Microsoft's latest console exclusive, Gears of War: E-Day , launched this week, and now we've gotten the first glimpse at how the game is performing commercially. Multiple analysts have weighed in, and there are numerous factors at play beyond pure sales, due to Game Pass and other factors. So let's break things down.

Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics released a report that said the game has sold about 230,000 copies so far, with Steam sales accounting for 168,000 and Xbox (across console and PC) making up the other 62,000.

Straight sales do not tell the whole story, though, because E-Day is available on Game Pass, which Elliott said "cannibalized" the majority of sales. He said Alinea's data showed than 1.7 million people acquired E-Day through their Game Pass subscription as opposed to buying a copy outright.

There is more nuance there, too, as Elliott said that 722,000 of the 1.7 million people who played E-Day through Game Pass bought the $30 Premium upgrade, which got them in early and awarded them with extra content.

"So despite selling far fewer copies on Steam, Xbox accounts for almost three-quarters of the revenue (roughly $26 million of the $37 million, versus about $11 million on Steam). So '230,000 copies' undersells the paying audience. Including the 722,000 upgrades, nearly 950,000 people actually paid something for E-Day."
Elliott concluded that these are "soft numbers" at a time "when Xbox badly needs revenue wins." In this environment, Elliott said E-Day's $70 edition is "functionally dead on Xbox."

"In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70. They paid $30 for five days early access to something they don’t own. Xbox is, in effect, charging its most valuable customers the least, based on a hangover from a tried-and-exhausted strategy from a previous administration," he said.
More to the story

Game Pass creates recurring revenue for Xbox, and it's big business. For the latest fiscal year, Game Pass brought in nearly $5 billion in revenue. E-Day's inclusion on Game Pass adds value to the service for Game Pass members.

However, Elliott said Game Pass is no longer growing, putting Xbox "at a crossroads." Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has alluded to this as well, saying Game Pass was one of Phil Spencer and Sarah Bond's big bets that did not pay off .
“Our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome,” she said.

Microsoft spent many billions of dollars acquiring numerous developers with the aim of funneling content to Game Pass. The strategy did not work , and now Xbox has made major changes to Game Pass, including removing the biggest day-one new release it ever had in the Call of Duty franchise. New releases are no longer included at launch, so players have to buy them outright or wait a year until they come to Game Pass.
"When a game this bloody awesome and well-reviewed [Gears of War: E-Day] does this softly on its home platform, the model--not the game--gets brought into question," Elliott said.

Mat Piscatella of Circana reminded people that E-Day's revenue was not totally cannibalized in practice through its inclusion on Game Pass because a person had to pay $23/month for Game Pass in the first place. Beyond that, Piscatella pointed out that that not everyone who played E-Day through Game Pass would buy the game outright if that was the only way.
What about a PS5 version?
Many people expected Microsoft to release E-Day on PS5, in part because Microsoft's own documents showed that a PS5 version was in the works and because Gears of War Reloaded came to PS5 a year ago.

A PS5 edition of E-Day was reportedly canceled at the last minute; Microsoft denied this, but no one believes that . Microsoft's Aaron Greenberg has said E-Day is not a timed exclusive for Xbox, meaning it may never come to PS5. However, he said the same thing about Starfield , and then it came to PS5, so people are understandably hesitant to believe what the company says.
Elliott previously said Gears of War: E-Day (along with Clockwork Revolution) are being sent out to die due to their exclusivity to Xbox. They are also coming to PC, but not PS5.
Elliott told GameSpot that Microsoft will never succeed in the console space and promising fans exclusive games to help drive console sales is not going to make a difference.

“Console as we know it is over for Xbox–and has been for a while. There’s no turning that ship. But they still need to pretend to care until they’ve transitioned to pastures where they can return to growth (if they succeed),” he said.

“A Gears console exclusive does not shift meaningful numbers of Series X units. Exclusivity as a hardware-driver is over for them, because the install base it would drive simply isn’t responsive enough to justify the cost of building hardware at a 5x component premium. And those games are on Steam anyway,” he added.
Elliott went on to say that Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution are “sacrificial lambs for hearts-and-minds, not economics.”
E-Day sequel possibilities

Will there be a sequel to E-Day? That remains to be seen, but The Coalition's Mike Crump said E-Day creates a "great foundation" for the franchise to grow. Crump also stated that a potential sequel could be made much faster. The studio has no other games in development that have been announced publicly.
Microsoft bought the Gears of War series from Epic in 2014 for an undisclosed sum.

There have been big changes at Xbox lately as part of Sharma's effort to "reset" the Xbox business and help it grow. This has included mass layoffs, studio closures, and game cancellations. Recently, Sharma said Xbox was at an " all time low" but is now growing again , though she didn't provide any data to support her claims.

news.title: Leisure Suit Larry is about to take his final bow
news.summary: The Wet Dreams games have been marked down dramatically ahead of their final removal from sale.

content.v: 2018's Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Don't Dry was a genuinely pleasant surprise, in that it's actually good—quite a contrast to the preceding games in the series, Magna Cum Laude and Box Office Bust, which were decidedly not good. A sequel followed, Wet Dreams Dry Twice , and once again it was pretty good stuff—not hugely innovative or high art, but a genuine Leisure Suit Larry experience that manages to avoid embarrassing itself (though it embarrasses Larry himself plenty).

Both of them, sadly, are soon going away for good. An announcement on Steam from publisher Assemble Entertainment says both games are being removed from the store on October 23. Ahead of that, they're being offered seriously cheap: 95% off the regular price, dropping them to less than $2 each.
The removal of the Wet Dreams duo effectively puts a pin in a process than began in 2025, when the OG Larry games were removed from sale:
Leisure Suit Larry 4 managed to avoid the executioner's axe by not existing in the first place .

A reason for this new round of delistings wasn't provided, nor did Assemble comment on the possibility of an eventual return. Expiring licenses rights are a common culprit for this sort of thing, and that seems to be a good bet here: Leisure Suit Larry was originally a Sierra game, which I assume means Assemble licensed the property from Activision for the Wet Dreams duo; given the timing (Wet Dreams Don't Dry was announced in 2018), we're coming up on roughly 10 years since that deal would've been done, which, as someone who's bad at math and thus likes nice round numbers, seems to me like a reasonably possible expiration date for such a deal.

But that's entirely speculation. What's certain is that Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Don't Dry and Wet Dreams Dry Twice are going away for good, and ahead of that they're both really cheap on both Steam and GOG—the delisting announcement makes no mention of their fate on GOG but it's a safe assumption they'll be disappeared there, too—until they're gone. Get 'em while they're wet.

news.title: Wardogs will bribe players with cash and XP to pick Blue team in Season 2
news.summary: "We're looking at how we can help the win rate of a certain team."

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/quGfuiKE7kHW9W8XDcB8yS.jpg
Blue team reinforcements

Bulkhead wants to boost one team's win rate, and it's willing to bribe its players (with in-game cash) to do it. Despite all three teams starting on equal grounds, many Wardogs players have been avoiding Blue from the start , going so far as to idle on the selection screen for minutes waiting for a slot to open on Green or Red.

The are practical balancing problems that work against Blue team, like their lackluster camouflage and unfavorable spawn points (Season 2 is tackling Bakurani), but the bonuses are meant to counter the other reason Blue sucks, as I covered last month:

"Another, less talked about possibility, is that Blue team's infamy is a self-fulfilling prophecy. Folks have one bad night with Lonestar and decide to believe the reputation, or hear it's the team to avoid, or notice everyone else actively avoiding it, and you end up with a Blue team full of less experienced players."

XP and cash bribes are a drastic move, but should have a real impact. It's unclear how big these boosts will be, but I expect Blue will instantly become the most popular team by a wide margin in Season 2.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/U9yqPBSZdjGNZrCFSwxKzH-1920-80.png

I wonder, though, if this problem wasn't slowly sorting itself out already. I've noticed the Blue bias dying down over the past couple weeks—the faction is still mostly losing in the NA West servers I frequent, but they're also scoring points and competing, which is a positive sign. I've even been on a couple of winning Blue teams, if you can believe it.

Wardogs Season 2 is shaping up to be bigger than I expected so soon after release. The October 15 patch also adds new guns, vehicles, rainy weather on all maps, and more to be revealed in the patch notes next week. It also marks the game's first progression wipe—everyone's going back to level 1.

news.title: Battlefield 6 Is Adding Something Fans Have Wanted Since Day 1
news.summary: EA and Battlefield Studios have unveiled more details on Battlefield 6 's upcoming Season 5, and it includes a

content.v: EA and Battlefield Studios have unveiled more details on Battlefield 6 's upcoming Season 5, and it includes a new feature that fans have wanted since day one: a proper server browser.

Battlefield did indeed launch with a server browser, but--considering how it only supported Portal mode--it wasn't the one fans wanted. One of the game's producers asked why players even want a full server browser. Now, in response to the feedback, Battlefield Studios is adding a proper server browser with the Season 5 update this December, allowing people to create their own servers and set rules like map rotation and other particulars . Classic-era Battlefield games had server browsers, and fans flocked to them because they could pick and choose exactly the maps and modes they wanted to play.

Season 5 rolls out in waves, beginning with Siege of Las Vegas on October 13, which adds two new maps: Vegas Strip and Area 51. For Battlefield 6's battle royale RedSec, Siege of Las Vegas adds a new version of the mode called Rapid Royale, which promises faster rounds with smaller player populations.

Battlefield 6's Season 5 will also include a Halloween event running October 20 through November 7, featuring a "limited-time scenario" that has players hunting down "secret tech" beneath Area 51. This scenario, which Battlefield Studios stressed is non-canon, includes a celebration of aliens and the Dead Space series, taking players to environments based on the 2023 remake. There will also be Dead Space-themed cosmetics to unlock.

Phase 2 of Season 5, called Casino Heist, begins November 10, adding a new map called European Casino. Finally, Phase 3, known as Frozen Aces, arrives on December 8, and as its name suggests, it will bring cold weather to Las Vegas, along with a new operation across the Vegas Strip and Area 51. The Battlefield 6 server browser also arrives during the Phase 3 of Season 5 .
Battlefield 6 was 2025's best-selling game in the US , even outperforming Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.

news.title: Wardogs Dev Says PS6 and Xbox Project Helix Ports Should Be Relatively Straightforward
news.summary: The team behind Wardogs expects to bring the game to next-gen consoles in the future.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2024/09/25/ps5-pro-handsonpreview-blogroll-1727223976585.jpg
The team behind Wardogs expects to bring the game to next-gen consoles in the future.

Although some would argue that this console generation has yet to meet its full potential, platform holders are already ramping up for the next one with Sony's PlayStation 6 and Xbox's Project Helix, though neither company has locked in an official release window. However, it does mean some developers have to start planning ahead, and one of those studios is Bulkhead, the team behind the new shooter Wardogs.

In an exclusive interview with IGN, we talked about plans for the game's eventual console release. Wardogs is currently slated to make the jump to consoles in 2028 , which begs the question: Will it release on next-gen hardware? Bulkhead says it's not even really a question.

"I think there's not too much to consider," said Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott. "We make the game performant, we're going to get it on the next-gen consoles. From our perspective, it's a straight port. So yeah, absolutely is the short answer, to be honest."

Senior producer Kane Allard noted that Bulkhead is already speaking with platform holders about the console versions of Wardogs, and doesn't anticipate any issues bringing the game to next-gen machines.

"We're obviously already in conversation with the proprietors of those platforms, and they're going to have certain criteria that we have to match, and I assume it's going to be the same for those other consoles as well. So from our perspective, if we get it on a base Xbox or base PlayStation, it shouldn't be much more work to get it on next-gen, and it should just be more performance. So I don't think it gives us anything new."

Last month, former PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida said Sony and Nintendo should make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs that have already prompted PS5 and Switch 2 price rises. Yoshida told The Verge that console companies needed to focus on sustaining their current hardware platforms for "as long as possible."

We know that a PS6 is on the way at some point . Previously, analysts had suggested a 2028 launch seemed likely, though Sony is yet to make any official indication of when PS6 may arrive — and as time goes on, that late 2028 release date feels less and less likely .

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has insisted Project Helix remains part of Microsoft's gaming plan, but has also said next-gen Xbox hardware will be a "family of devices." "We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10," she said in a memo reported by Windows Central . "There is not one device that fits all. We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that will we partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."

For now, anyone looking to play Wardogs will have to check out the PC version, which is currently in early access. Next week sees the launch of Season 2 , which will introduce major gameplay features such as rain.

news.title: Dungeons & Dragons Is Going to Outer Space With Star Wars: Tyro Squadron, First Look at Official Art
news.summary: Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft isn't even out yet, but Wizards of the Coast has already announced its n

Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft isn't even out yet, but Wizards of the Coast has already announced its next Universes Beyond release for the TTRPG – and it's Star Wars.

WotC announced that something Star Wars was coming to D&D back at Gen Con in July, but at NYCC 2026, it confirmed a new adventure, Star Wars: Tyro Squadron, along with a new Core Rules expansion for the Galaxy Far, Far Away.

The new Core Rules will likely be as large in scope as the recent World of Warcraft expansion, with a ton of story hooks and new ways to play classic D&D classes, but we don't know anything specific. news.title: Wardogs Dev Holding Back Certain Features Because of Xbox Series S, but Working to 'Very Low-End Hardware' Has Its Benefits
news.summary: The developer of Wardogs has admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S have stopped it from adding ce

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2022/11/30/seriess-1624390081463-1669817083526.jpg

The developer of Wardogs has admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S have stopped it from adding certain things to the game, but insisted these limits have also provided some unique benefits.

During a press conference for Wardogs Season 2, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer said the team is "limited" by the Xbox Series S and revealed that this is one of the reasons why the game doesn't have dynamic weather right now. The new rain feature being added to Wardogs this month will be persistent throughout a match, meaning a storm won't suddenly roll through halfway through a game and lighten up within 15 minutes. It's a constant downpour.

"We are limited, as every dev is, by Xbox Series S," said Brammer. "As great a platform as Xbox is, it's a very low-end hardware for a game like Wardogs. We have to be mindful of these things we're putting in the game now. Performance is the reason we don't do it, but we would love to see it at some point. There's an ambition for it, but nobody is working on it right now."

Bulkhead isn't the first team to acknowledge difficulties around Microsoft's cheaper console, which launched alongside the Xbox Series X in November 2020. Moon Studio founder Thomas Mahler stated earlier this year that it was delaying No Rest for the Wicked's Xbox release due to troubles with the Xbox Series S . Baldur's Gate 3 also came to Xbox a few months late and required the help of Microsoft's engineers to get the game's split-screen co-op working on Series S .

Indeed, one of the questions facing Microsoft ever since the release of the Xbox Series S is whether it would be willing to allow developers and publishers to release a game on Xbox Series X only, leaving Xbox Series S behind. As it stands, Xbox mandates that video games launch on both or none at all, and that there should be main feature parity between each version.

Although Wardogs isn't coming to console until 2028 , Bulkhead is hyper-aware of how everything it puts in the game could impact consoles in the future. In a follow-up interview exclusive to IGN, studio co-founder Howard Philpott echoed sentiments about possibly adding dynamic weather in the future, but noted Bulkhea would have to handle it carefully to avoid tanking performance. He added that, while Series S has its pitfalls, it also lets the developer optimize the game for lower-end PCs.

"As for Series S, Joe is right, and it's not an industry secret or anything," he said. "It is holding back what developers can do in terms of pushing the boundaries because it's so far behind par in terms of the rest of the power of the rest of the consoles. So yeah, it's something we have to be cognizant of, but at the same time, Series S does actually give us that baseline performance.

"We were so heavy [during] pre-release in terms of talking about performance for PC, and what we didn't necessarily talk about [during the] press conference was how much Series S drove us to make the performance good on lower-spec PCs, because the goal is to get everyone to be able to play with all of their friends. There's an obvious financial benefit to that, so it's not completely altruistic, but at the same time, it is the goal. That is the point of the game: being able to play with as many people as possible."

Philpott also noted that Bulkhead has always imagined Wardogs as a multi-platform game. The team recognized there was heavy demand for controller support prior to Wardogs' early access launch, prompting them to quickly put something together. He stated that this support is in "an okay serviceable state, but really it needs to be a lot better." Senior producer Kane Allard noted that situation has prompted Bulkhead to be more "forward thinking."

"I think that's a good example of one of the things that bit us a bit and made us realize actually we do need to be forward thinking," said Allard. "We made the decision, as Howard said, originally we were releasing on PC for early access, and it was kind of an afterthough, we need to have controller support. And then we realized there was a massive outcry for it, and we had to look back at the systems we had and try and make them work with controller, and there was a fair amount of work there. And yeah, we did do it in the end and it was a little bit of a slog, but that did burn us a bit. And we then realized, yeah, we need to be really smart, build stuff with console in mind, with controller in mind, and we're taking that forward for everything that we put in the game."

It will be a while before Wardogs makes its way to consoles, but this is a major part of the game's journey. Philpott also said that Bulkhead hired a pro Halo player to help with controller support and ensuring that it gets an extra level of care.
Wardogs Season 2 will launch next week on October 15.

news.title: Wardogs Dev Explains Why Blue Team Loses More, Confirms Plan to Address the Balance in Season 2
news.summary: The team behind Wardogs has confirmed that Lonestar, AKA the blue team, loses more than other teams and is mak

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/09/s02-patchnotes-flakpanzer-gepard-1791560561425.png
The team behind Wardogs has confirmed that Lonestar, AKA the blue team, loses more than other team, and is making big changes in Season 2 to fix that.

Since Wardogs launched in early September, there have been no shortage of memes mocking the game's blue team, Lonestar. For whatever reason, Lonestar tends to lose a lot, and there are a plethora of videos showing Lonestar players crashing helicopters at base and making fools of themselves.

Speaking exclusively with IGN, Bulkhead confirmed that Lonestar's win percentage is lower than other teams in Wardogs, but it has actually increased over time. Lonestar's win rate was roughly 10% during the game's alpha, but has risen to 20% in recent weeks. Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott noted that this is partially a result of players choosing to support Lonestar because they see it as an underdog challenge. He even joked that blue team's reputation was a bit of a PR issue.

"So originally, and this is key to not misquote, it was like 10% in the alpha," he said. "So that then led to the perception: blue is bad, don't join blue. And then everyone tries to click on green and click on red because they're competitive and they want to win. So they're going on the better team. More recently, it's closer to 15 to 20%. It's probably closer to 20% right now, where people have actively been joining blue team to try and make them win, which is quite entertaining to watch. But it's undeniable, they are losing more than the other two teams because of that perception."

Bulkhead is taking steps to remedy this with the launch of Season 2 next week . The biggest change is that they are adjusting spawns and rebuilding bases for all teams on the map Bakurani. Senior producer Kane Allard noted that blue team's reputation may have been compounded by the fact that they were losing significantly more on Bakurani, possibly due to map issues. As a result, they've chosen to shake up all of the spawns.

"We've moved all three spawns, so it's not just blue team have moved," said Allard. "It's blue, red, and green. They've all moved. The actual hot zone of Bakurani hasn't been changed. It's just the spawn zones. It's kind of revitalized the map, and we've seen from a data standpoint with our internal tests that it has evened it out. But yeah, as Howard said, there is a genuine PR issue with Lonestar, and there are a few extra things that we're going to be doing to hopefully help turn the tide of that, as well."

Some of those "few extra things" include changing the saturation on Lonestar's uniforms so they can blend in better, cash and XP bonuses for playing and winning as Lonestar, and even posters in the other teams' spawns encouraging other players to switch to blue team.
"Yeah, we are doing some fun stuff," said Philpott. "We're even putting posters like 'Lonestar needs you,' in the other teams' spawns. So yeah, it should be good fun."

In a press conference, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer joked that, "if you're not playing blue team, you are in fact, a pu**y." So with that said, it is now up to the players to take these buffs and changes to try and change the perception of Lonestar.
Wardogs Season 2 launches on October 15.

news.title: Wardogs' New Rain System Will Have a Major Effect on Gameplay in Season 2
news.summary: Wardogs developer Bulkhead has revealed how rain will change the gameplay in Season 2.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/09/s02-trailer-stills1-1791560517450.png
Wardogs developer Bulkhead has revealed how rain will change the gameplay in Season 2.

Next week, Wardogs will release its second season of content, which will also add rain to the game. This will not be dynamic weather, so don't expect it to be sunshine one minute and storming the next; matches that include rain will experience rainfall the entire time, from start to finish. However, this will result in some major changes to the game, with senior producer Kane Allard confirming to IGN that it "completely changes the game," and as a result, some players may not actually like this addition.

"It completely changes the game, and it's going to be positive for some players," said Allard. "It's going to be negative for others. Your play styles might be affected. That's okay. It's not like every map's going to be permanently rain. It's just going to be almost like a different game mode, so to speak. [It] could be that some people really love rain, some people really hate rain based on how you want to play. But it does bring a lot."

As for how things change, it's pretty drastic. The map is obviously darker, and your visibility is worsened. One developer even stated that he lost his sense of direction on the map because he wasn't used to the way it looked now. The storms will cause thunder, which can be strategically used to mask gunfire or other loud noises. Raindrops will make different sounds based on the surfaces they're hitting, including rooftops and helmets. Windows will also fog up, though it's unclear if that allows players to be less visible when hiding in buildings. The team has also accounted for destruction, meaning if a roof is destroyed, players inside will be exposed to the rain.

As for other weather effects, Bulkhead isn't ruling anything out, but it has to consider how something like snow would change the game both in terms of gameplay and how the game performs. Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer stated that there are obvious changes to something like nighttime, which would add flashlights, NVGs, and lasers. Maybe one day we'll get more, but it sounds like it may take some time to get added.
We've got plenty more on Wardogs, including Bulkhead on why blue team loses more, a new gambling mechanic for Season 2, and even word of a next-gen port. Wardogs Season 2 launches on October 15.

news.title: Wardogs Season 2 Adds a New Gambling Mechanic That Lets You Bet on Yourself
news.summary: Wardogs Season 2 is adding a new gambling system which will allow players to bet on their own performance.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/09/s02-trailer-stills3-1791560662296.png
Wardogs Season 2 is adding a new gambling system that will allow players to bet on their own performances.

The new season of Wardogs, due to launch on October 15, features a bunch of new content, most notably a new weather system that adds rain to matches . Another major mechanic lets players win big, or lose tons of cash. It's called the Wager Vendor, and it allows players to bet on themselves. If you think you can kill 20 people in a match, make a bet, and you will be rewarded. However, if you fail, you will lose cash. The harder your challenge is, the more you stand to win.

Speaking exclusively to IGN about the new system, developer Bulkhead noted that it technically won't be available to players as soon as the season launches, as they'll have to unlock it by building up cash.

"The Wager Vendor basically lets you bet on your own performance," said Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott. "So if I want to go in and say, 'I'm going to get 20 kills this match,' you then set that in your Wager Vendor, you then set the condition so I can say, 'Oh, I need to go and kill 20 people with my fists.' Okay, that's a bit harder, but that's when the odds go up. And then you set that as a condition and you can add multiple conditions."
"If you're a really good player and you're really smart about building your wager, you can make big money, but you can also lose big money," added senior producer Kane Allard.
Players can get pretty specific with these wagers. However, the more restrictions you put on yourself, the harder it will be to accomplish.

"Conditions-wise, it can even go down to as minute as, 'I need to get five kills, they're all head shots, all with the AK74M, and they all have to be in the hot zone, and my loadout has to cost less than 20K,'" said Allard. "You can build that wager and you can maybe earn double of what you put down, but that's a lot of restrictions that you're putting on yourself, and there's going to be players that may be also trying the same thing, and it just adds a little bit more tension to the game."

This not only spices up the gameplay, but it can also be extremely rewarding for players who are trying to build up some cash. If you're playing medic, you could theoretically give yourself a bonus for reviving 30 players. This then incentivizes medics to help their team more. It'll be intersting to see how this changes player behavior, but it sounds like it could be a lot of fun.

Call of Duty had a far less detailed version of this system in 2010's Call of Duty: Black Ops. Players could unlock items with an in-game currency and go into high stakes party games, such as Gun Game and One in the Chamber, to try and earn more money. GTA Online also has a betting system, allowing players to bet on players they think will perform best in PvP modes.

Battlefield 6 is getting a Dead Space event in time for Halloween. EA and Dice are calling it a “non-canon” event, which means the Battlefield 6 developer can go wild with it. Necromorphs in Area 51? Why not?

The Dead Space and Battlefield 6 crossover was teased earlier in the week, with the alien monument The Marker showing up at the end of the shooter’s Vegas trailer. Pax Armata will be pursuing secret tech hidden beneath Area 51 in the event, which will be decked out with assets taken from the Dead Space remake .
Players will be able to unlock unique cosmetics for participating, starting when the event goes live on October 20. You’ll have until November 7 to grab what you want.

“Battlefield 6 is now one year old and what an incredible journey it’s been, from our Top Gun collaboration, which coincided with the return of Naval Warfare, to the launch of some of the most exhilarating maps in Battlefield history,” Battlefield Studios general manager Patrick Klaus said.

“And we’re just getting started, with Season 5 set to be the biggest yet. This has been an unforgettable year and we can’t thank players enough. We’re ending 2026 with a bang with three maps set in and around Las Vegas, a new way to experience REDSEC, as well as delivering on some of our community’s most requested features, with the introduction of Platoons and Server Browser. The new season sees players wage war across the Vegas strip, peppering the neon skyline with hot lead and baking under the desert sun. The area 51 map will also be playable across standard modes.

news.title: Street Fighter Was On Death’s Door, And Its Players Weren’t Getting Any Younger
news.summary: Street Fighter 5 launched in 2016 in rough shape, and if things hadn't changed, the classic fighting game fran

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/08/04/sf6-outfits-blog-1754304622675.jpg

Street Fighter 6 producer Shuhei Matsumoto revealed how dire things were for Capcom’s flagship fighting game franchise during the Street Fighter V era and explained how he and director Takayuki Nakayama worked together to save the series from death.

It’s no secret that Street Fighter V stumbled massively when it launched in February 2016. Many players felt that it was shipped out in an unfinished state, as it lacked basic elements like an arcade mode or story mode, on top of its incredibly unstable netplay.

Shuhei Matsumoto — who stepped in as producer for Street Fighter V near the end of its lifetime following Yoshinori Ono’s exit from Capcom in 2020 — alongside director Takayuki Nakayama, recognized that the franchise as a whole was in peril, and believed that the Street Fighter IP might actually fade into obscurity within the next decade if they didn’t act fast.

"When the two of us were talking during Street Fighter V, we realized that if we didn't do something about Street Fighter, the Street Fighter IP would probably die in 10 years. It was critical. So, we had to make it a game where people would get to know it all over again and play it again,” Matsumoto said during an October 2026 interview with Karin Ohira .
Matsumoto explained that SFV’s aging playerbase was one example of this issue, saying Capcom needed to target younger players if it wanted Street Fighter to live.

"At that time, the player base for Street Fighter V was roughly 35 to 45 years old. In 10 years, these people will be 60. It’s difficult to sustain the franchise if we only rely on that group,” he continued.

"...It had become a distant presence. People knew of the scene, but weren't actually playing the game, which made us think, 'This is bad.' In the end, we're a game company, yet people weren't playing our game. Isn't that the most fatal thing? So that was the biggest danger. We didn't know if those people would continue with the same level of passion, and naturally, there's a lifespan to things, right? That's when we talked about how, if we left it as it was, the IP would likely die in 10 years."

So, how did they manage to turn things around so dramatically with Street Fighter 6 ? Matsumoto said that the team avoided relying on its power as a historic IP, and decided to start with a blank slate, as if no one in the current generation knew about it, at all.

"While people say Street Fighter has high name recognition, we shouldn't be overconfident. We decided to act as if the current generation doesn't know us. We have to properly explain things to those who are just starting to play games now — like who these characters are and how to play — so we don't take that familiarity for granted."

Matsumoto also said that the development of SF6's Modern control scheme was integral to reaching a new audience, alongside other approachable features like World Tour Mode (which has since been paused for the forseeable future), the Battle Hub, and real-time commentary from community figures like Vicious and Tasty Steve.

Matsumoto and Nakayama’s plan paid off big time; Street Fighter 6 is one of Capcom’s most successful Street Fighter games of all time, having sold more than seven million lifetime units as of summer 2026. It’s extremely popular both in Japan and abroad, and boasts a massive playerbase across both Steam and consoles.

It’s a big year for Street Fighter fans and Capcom in general; the developer has released three critically-acclaimed titles in Resident Evil Requiem , Pragmata , and Onimusha: Way of the Sword , and is gearing up for the Street Fighter movie on October 16, which comes on the heels of the Resident Evil adaptation directed by horror savant Zach Cregger.

news.title: Worldwide PC shipments have plummeted by over 20%, to the surprise of absolutely no one
news.summary: Could it be something to do with.... the memory crisis?

content.v: IDC Research has released its figures regarding worldwide PC shipments in the third quarter of 2026, and would you believe it, they've dropped considerably. Looking at the year-over-year numbers, the shipped units dropped from 78.5 million in Q3 2025, to 62.7 million in Q3 of this year. That's a 20.1% plummet, for percentage fans.

But why, I hear you asking. Actually, I don't. The memory and supply chain crisis, driven by AI server demand is pinpointed by the IDC as the primary driver of the decline, which will come as no surprise to those of us in non-rock-based abodes.

However, it's worth looking a bit deeper into exactly what's happened here. The "pull-in" of stock created by vendors buying up supply in the first half of this year (in anticipation of the forecasted price hikes) has essentially borrowed volume from the second half, according to the report. As a result, this boosted the early year shipments and "left Q3 starved of demand."

"The result is a broken seasonal pattern: the third quarter is normally larger than the second, and this year it fell short," says the IDC. It's bad out there folks—and this report predicts that things might get gloomier for the industry in the near future.

"Channel concern over high inventory and soft demand at elevated prices could bring promotions in the near term, but pricing will stay well above year-ago levels," the report continues. "The bigger risk is macro: conditions have worsened since last quarter, and a weaker economic backdrop could push demand lower and darken the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027"
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MgyYMxJjwmrmG9bY7mRfVg-1920-80.jpg

I love writing good news stories. It's a shame I don't get a whole lot of them these days. My heart almost leapt when I read this quote from IDC research director Jitesh Ubrani: "Channels are now worried about carrying too much inventory into a market where high prices are suppressing demand. That could translate into promotions and some short-term relief for consumers..."

Then dropped again at the second half of the sentence: "... but we don’t expect pricing anywhere near what it was a year ago. Prices will remain elevated. With macro conditions worsening, the risk is that the outlook for the next few quarters gets worse before it gets better."

Anyway, the report also points out that this economic pain was not felt evenly, as Lenovo, HP, and Dell fell faster than the market and collectively lost 4.2 points of share, with HP being the hardest hit, dropping from 19.1% to 16.5%.

Lenovo is still the biggest shipper of PCs overall , though, and the three companies keep their same positions in the rankings as they did this time last year, with HP coming in second and Dell in third. In fourth position is Apple, which has also seen an 11.3% drop in growth, and in fifth place comes Asus, with its own growth figures dropping by 8.6%.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/NRiuWJ8YersHWaELvtB9vj-1920-80.jpg

Well, I don't think any of us can say we're shocked to hear this news. With the crisis continually predicted to worsen from those in the know, (like Micron's CEO, who recently took the opportunity to ram that point home over and over again ), it looks like PC pricing is screwed for a while to come yet. "Promotions are possible," the report handily sums up. "However, prices are expected to remain elevated and well above where they were at the same time last year."

In a totally unrelated question, did you buy a PC recently, and are you interested in letting it go for a reasonable sum? Asking for a friend. No pressure, take your time, I can wait here, etc, etc. Got any spare memory modules while we're at it?

news.title: 'It's Every Motherf***er for Himself!' — The San Andreas Mission You Need to Play Before GTA 6
news.summary: GTA San Andreas' Reuniting the Families mission has car chases, shootouts, and cops recreating Terminator 2. I

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/08/sa-aotl-blog-1791457650959.jpg

When Rockstar debuted its extended look at GTA 6 on Netflix, it was as if the developer had uploaded a one-off episode of a crime thriller to the platform. Sure, this was a gameplay reveal and there was certainly plenty of what was clearly a person playing a video game, but it nonetheless felt like a cinematic event. Compelling characters, building tension, slick action, and beautiful camera direction – it was as if Michael Mann had shadow-dropped a CGI short.

None of that will have come as a surprise. Rockstar has always had one eye on the movies – the game that shot it to stardom is a love-letter to Goodfellas, and its most recent open-world is the greatest Western never filmed. But the cinematic ambition we associate with the studio truly came to fruition in 2004 with Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas . Its predecessors, GTA 3 and Vice City, had been packed with references to classic crime cinema and voiced by genuine Hollywood talent. But that wasn’t enough for San Andreas. For this ‘90s-set Californian epic, Rockstar wanted to put you in the movies. And so it designed missions that felt like they’d been pulled from the silver screen.

There’s no better example of this than Reuniting the Families, the penultimate chapter of San Andreas’ opening act. It’s a highly-scripted, expertly directed slice of interactive storytelling that casts you in the leading role. And by trading the freedom of its open world for a tighter, more authored experience, San Andreas makes this gripping getaway feel more dramatic than any story the series had told thus far.

It remains true even today that the vast majority of Grand Theft Auto’s missions take place outdoors. This is a series built on the city sandbox. One of its most appealing facets is that you’re free to go anywhere – every road, alley, and freeway is fair game. Causing trouble in that mass sprawl of concrete and asphalt was simply what GTA was during the first two games of the series’ 3D era, which for the most part only permitted you to come indoors when an NPC invited you in for a cutscene.

But the indoors offers something the open-world can't: Control. Direction. Oversight. Rooms and corridors are the perfect container for scenes and set-pieces, untouched by the continual simulation of metropolitan life. And so it’s no surprise that San Andreas, with its substantially loftier storytelling goals, frequently sends you into buildings all over its digital golden state. As Carl “CJ” Johnson, you stealthily murder your way through a music mogul’s mansion, steal rifles from a sleeping weapons hoarder, and rescue a damsel in distress from a burning condo – all moments that, thanks to a stronger guiding hand and purposeful level design, feel akin to playing through a movie scene.

That feeling peaks in Reuniting the Families, a turning point for the failing Grove Street gang. With the rival Ballas having practically overrun the city of Los Santos with its drug pushing operation, CJ’s brother Sweet decides it’s time to pull together the gang’s fractured families. He’ll meet the heads of the sets at the Jefferson Motel. CJ and fellow gang members Ryder and Smoke will accompany him, but remain outside while the negotiations take place. Soon, a rejuvenated Grove Street will strike back at their enemies and reclaim the streets.

If only crime were that simple. As soon as Sweet enters the building, the police turn up in force. Ryder and Smoke scarper – “It’s every motherf*cker for himself!” – but CJ heads into the motel to rescue his brother.

Confined by the complex’s small rooms and enclosed hallways, San Andreas suddenly transforms from an open-world playground into a third-person shooter. The motel’s layout functions akin to a level in a linear video game, its corridors guiding you forward through a series of pre-determined moments and combat encounters. The tense atmosphere this scripting creates is apparent from the moment you load in – a fellow Grove Street member is shot to pieces and sent flailing over the hall’s upper balcony. Another lies dead in the stairwell. A woman runs for her life. As you head on up to the main floor, you’re hit by an unexpected jump scare: a SWAT officer rolls through the door and opens fire. You’re about to enter a criminal's worst nightmare, a house of horrors where the law is waiting to pop out from behind every door.

The motel’s corridors are lined with invisible trigger points, each one kickstarting a unique scenario that turns a generic video game shootout into a cinematic vision of a building under siege. A civilian runs from one room to another, crossing your line of fire. A door blows off its hinges. Gangsters light up troopers as they crash through a skylight. An officer hangs from an air vent to take you by surprise. As you inch forward through this maze of rent-by-the-hour rooms, it becomes clear that each square foot of it has been painstakingly crafted to ensure every second of the ordeal feels ripped from the movies. Unlike the movies, though, there’s no guarantee that the hero will survive. You still need to demonstrate some skill to stay alive.

Thankfully, CJ is no slouch; he can combat roll just as good as a pig in kevlar. This is the tool that will shift you in and out of cover, taking you from safety to a perfect firing position in just a couple of incredibly cool seconds. And there is a lot of cover – not just the 90-degree corridor corners, but laundry baskets, sofas, and upturned tables. This is a cover shooter map built two years before Gears of War made chest-high walls a trend. Naturally, such an arrangement demands an appropriate weapon. Armed with the MP5 that his enemies drop, CJ becomes John McClaine, the motel his own miniature Nakatomi Tower. Now I have a machine gun, ho ho ho.

After creating a small mountain of corpses, CJ finally reunites with Sweet and the pair make their escape. A rooftop showdown with a police helicopter would, in any other mission, act as the finale, but this isn’t any other mission. Sending the whirlybird to its doom is just the half way point. With every cop in the city on your tail, a lifeline is found in Smoke and Ryder, who suddenly pull up in getaway wheels. There’s no time to question where they’ve been or why they’ve returned to the scene of the bust. You hop in and call shotgun. Well, AK – you’ll need fully automatic fire for this one.

The mission’s second half sees the format shift from third-person shooter to on-rails turret sequence. And while the action has spilled out into the streets, the tight control allowed by an interior space remains: technically speaking, CJ is inside a car, its driver following Rockstar’s script to the letter. The journey is completely authored, and so it becomes a rollercoaster ride through Los Santos – the route specifically designed to take you through streets perfectly shaped for the oncoming storm.

Police cruisers give chase, their passengers pumping magazine after magazine into your car’s bodywork. Initially, you’re at the front of the pack, the boys in blue tailing behind, but that very quickly changes. Like a city-sized Disneyland dark ride, cops keep popping up on either side of the track – screeching out of alleyways or thundering through junctions. What begins as a simple “blast what’s behind you” becomes a 360-degree shooting gallery, demanding constant assessment of all angles for incoming threats.

news.title: Valve is telling devs how well their games actually run on Steam Deck with real world data
news.summary: Here's hoping devs actually use those figures to improve compatibility.

content.v: Have you ever clicked on a Steam Deck Verified game, attempted to boot it up, and realised it probably shouldn't have been verified? Well, Steam's new system should help developers give a more accurate understanding of how their games run on the Steam Deck.

As of October 1 (via TechPowerUp ), Valve has given developers access to frame rate data as reported by Steam Deck users. A developer can see the frame rate that users are playing at as a percentage of sessions, meaning they can see if it runs well (at the Steam Deck's usual 60/90 fps cap) or not (users are generally lowering the fps limit).

That does mean it's only data willingly shared, and there are some caveats. The LCD Steam Deck has a max refresh rate of 60, while the OLED model goes up to 90. As games are often capped for fps to save resources, that will shape the stats somewhat. In addition, it can't guarantee how Steam Deck owners use their devices.

That being said, giving access to a high enough volume of data means that the fps averages should balance out in a bell curve, assuming enough players opt in. Valve claims "a majority of Steam Deck players have opted in".

The major benefit of this update is that developers can see how their games run on a mass of Steam Decks, and therefore adjust graphical options. This could be particularly valuable in games like Cyberpunk 2077 that have a dedicated Steam Deck mode. If developers notice those on handhelds aren't getting 60 fps or can't hit a smooth 30 average fps, they might tweak the settings a tad.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kLev9og6m9wsaoHX9JDQMU-1920-80.jpg
Valve has even explained that Steam Deck data is just a "starting point for iteration as we learn what sorts of data and presentation are useful."

That means, if successful, other devices could get the same data grouping. If enough Legion Go S users submit their data, or sales of the Steam Machine are high enough, it could get valuable data to developers.
This is, however, assuming that developers will tweak games for these devices. It only works for verified games, so it can't be used as part of the verification process as of right now.

Still, if mass reports of poor performance on Steam Deck start coming in for verified games, this means devs can really dig into the numbers to see what the average player is experiencing. Devs can then see in real time where updates positively or negatively impact performance. More data is always a good thing in my book.

news.title: WoW: Forever dev says 'there's a real longing for that slower, more deliberate pace' in MMOs: 'A deliberate pushback on this go go go nature'
news.summary: "It could be something with the times that we live in."

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever has me in a chokehold, and it's partially because—well, it's relaxing. As my colleague at PC Gamer so succinctly put it: "Sometimes it's fun to hit a scorpion with a club for 38 seconds." Despite aping an era seen as more 'hardcore' to some players, Forever's lack of blaring and annoying seasonal grist is honestly refreshing.

Speaking with associate production director Clay Stone about why I'm certainly not the only one feeling that way (given the success of Classic, Season of Discovery, and now Forever's beta), he says it's a question Blizzard's been considering "for a little while.

"We saw, certainly with the success of Classic and the response to that, it was more than just a nostalgic experience for some people. The fact that they didn't leave, you know? They didn't just play for a month. They fell in love with it all over again. Then we saw it again a lot with Hardcore in 2023. All of a sudden, now you had a whole bunch of people who'd never played the game before, but were coming in because of that slower pace, and the fact that Hardcore reinforced that slower pace for them."

But it's more than just about the pace of levelling—it's also about the wider structure, too. Retail WoW is a seasonal game, which certainly has both benefits and drawbacks . One such drawback being that if you miss the start of a season, you're kind of put off the whole exercise:

"We had so many players who didn't even play Season of Discovery simply because it was a Season, even though they had friends who were saying 'this is the best version of World of Warcraft that they've ever made!' But because it was a season, it felt ephemeral, and therefore [people thought] 'I'm not going to jump in'."

Forever, in many ways, feels like an extrapolation of Season of Discovery—the Classic+ of it all—in a package that's not going anywhere. Personally, I fear for my free time, because even knowing my beta character's going to be deleted, I just can't seem to pull myself away. And it is, again, because of that zenlike state—the modern world is busy, which makes hitting satyrs chill by comparison.

"It could be something with the times that we live in," says Stone. "The amount of information and noise that we're facing all the time, the distractions of all the notifications on my phone that are blaring at me everyday, but there's a real longing for that slower, more deliberate pace.

"And I think something that we've seen over these past few weeks, which I'm really happy to see, is that players who are coming into WoW Forever, whether they played World of Warcraft before or not, are trying themselves not to rush it. There seems to be a deliberate pushback on this 'go go go' nature."

That's not to say Stone's anti-go go go entirely, though. Even in the beta, I've seen plenty of folks min-maxxing or trying to reach for bis, which has its own charm: "We love them too. We think that they're great, and the endgame is going to be spectacular.

"But we're deliberately trying to build something with WoW Forever that answers that question of… 'Is it too late to start?' With an emphatic 'no' as much as possible." Horizontal progression, baby—it worked out for Guild Wars 2 , and I'm excited to see Blizzard take a crack at it as well.
